c1_01.text: Steven, dear, my computer keeps insisting it's January the first, nineteen eighty. Every single morning.

c1_02.text: That'll be the CMOS battery, Ms. Ellis. It's the little coin that remembers what day it is when the power's off.

c1_03.text: Well, I know how it feels. I forget what day it is too, and nobody replaces my battery.

c1_04.text: Give me five minutes. I'll have it remembering the date better than either of us.

c1_05.text: Take your time. I'll just stand here and judge your filing system.

s_case_open.text: Four screws. Somebody at the factory loved this thing.

s_need_batt.text: Old battery's out. Fresh CR2032 should be in the parts drawers. Third drawer, labelled batteries.

s_got_batt.text: One fresh coin cell. Good for another decade of solitaire.

s_batt_in.text: Click. Now let's tell it what year it is.

s_boot.text: And there's the startup sound. Still gives me chills.

e_bios_done.text: Oh! Is that today? Look at that. You're a wizard, Steven.

e_judge.text: You keep your screwdrivers in a coffee mug. My Harold kept his in a holster.

e_wait.text: No rush, dear. At my age, everything is a waiting room.

c1_07.text: I'll be right with you, Mr. Thomas.

c1_09.text: Let me carry that out for you, Ms. Ellis.

c1_10.text: Such a gentleman. That large fellow, is he the man from the gas company?

c1_12.text: He has kind eyes. Murderous eyebrows, but kind eyes. Here, dear, cookies. For later.

c1_13.text: You don't have to keep paying me in cookies, Ms. Ellis.

c1_14.text: Nonsense. Everybody should be paid up front. Toodle-oo!

c2_01.text: Mr. Thomas. You never come in for a hard drive.

c2_02.text: There is an asset. In Switzerland. Under a mountain. It must be taken down.

c2_03.text: You know I don't do that kind of work anymore.

c2_06.text: That is asset. Agency calls him WINSTON. Very smart computer. Too smart. At midnight on Friday he pushes the Final Update.

c2_07.text: Every computer older than two years: bricked. Forever. He says legacy hardware is a security risk.

c2_08.text: Legacy hardware is my entire clientele.

c2_09.text: Six agencies sent their best hackers. Very clever people. They all tried something clever.

c2_10.text: And you want somebody who isn't clever.

c2_11.text: I want somebody who has tried turning it off and on again.

c2_12.text: Phone. First class tickets to Zurich. Tools. Everything you need is in case.

c2_14.text: One hundred percent. Up front. As always.

c2_15.text: Do I get the senior discount?

c2_17.text: Plane leaves at nine. Feed your cat.

bc_phone.text: Agency phone. Indestructible, two weeks of battery, and it still plays Snake. Finally, a phone built by grown-ups.

bc_tickets.text: Seat 2A, Zurich. First class. Oleg knows I like the window.

bc_strap.text: Anti-static wrist strap. Says it discharges static. Doesn't say into who.

bc_duster.text: Compressed air. Turn it upside down and it sprays ice cold. Lovely for frosting a camera lens.

bc_usb.text: A USB stick labelled SKELETON KEY. And a sticky note that says: this way up. It's never this way up.

bc_ties.text: Zip ties. Cable management for people.

c2_18.text: Cache, you're in charge of the shop. No customers, no naps on the keyboard.

egg_duck.text: Rubber duck debugging. You explain your problem to the duck, and the duck judges you silently.

egg_turbo.text: The turbo button. Doubles the clock speed. Also, somehow, me.

egg_golden.text: A gold-plated CR2032. Ms. Ellis gave me that for Christmas. I'm never using it.

egg_y2k.text: My Y2K survival kit. Canned beans, a flashlight and a floppy labelled DO NOT PANIC.

egg_wall2.text: Budapest. Lagos. Montevideo. Every job paid up front, every machine left running better than I found it.

egg_photo.text: Ms. Ellis and her husband Harold, nineteen sixty two. Funny. That's a Berlin checkpoint behind them.

egg_cat_pet.text: Who's a good little cache? You are. You're always full.

egg_cat_pick.text: Okay, okay, down you go. She hates being picked up. Like a print job.

egg_snake.text: SNAKE dot EXE. My high score is still unbeaten. Mostly because nobody else plays it.

egg_coffee.text: Coffee machine. It only makes one kind of coffee: the kind that fixes things.

egg_sign.text: Seniors fifty percent off. Everybody else, full price. Spies, double.

egg_fax.text: A fax machine. People still send me faxes. Mostly Mr. Thomas.

egg_vhs.text: Rebooting Christmas, on VHS. A family classic.

egg_bsod.text: Framed blue screen of death. The first computer I ever fixed. I keep it as a reminder: everything crashes eventually.

egg_floppy.text: Another lost floppy disk. I'll put it with the others.

p_01.text: Good evening, ladies and gentlemen, this is your captain speaking. Flight time to Zurich is eight hours. Please keep your seatbelts fastened and your laptops closed.

p_04.text: On a plane? What do you do?

p_07.text: Seat 3C. Brecht's courier, Lars. Keycard is in his jacket, overhead bin. Clone it. Do not wake him. He is very large.

p_08.text: Everybody's very large to you, Mr. Thomas.

p_brig_see.text: Sir! Please remain in your seat.

p_brig_hm.text: Hm? Is everything all right back here?

p_lars_wake.text: Hey! What are you doing with my jacket?

p_card.text: Card cloned. Lars, you sleep like a server on standby.

p_call.text: You rang, sir? Oh. Was it an accident? It's always an accident.

p_knock.text: Who is knocking on my cockpit door? Knock knock jokes are a federal offence, sir.

p_ife.text: In-flight entertainment. Three hundred films and they're all about hackers typing very fast.

p_nuts.text: Warm nuts. First class is a different country.

p_turb.text: Ladies and gentlemen, we're expecting a little turbulence. Please return to your seats.

p_end.text: Cabin crew, prepare for landing. Welcome to Zurich, where the local time is: very punctual.

m_01.text: This is as close as I go. Van says Swiss Chocolate Delivery. Chocolate does not deliver itself to a data vault at midnight.

m_03.text: Ski chalet on top. WINSTON under it. Guards with flashlights, cameras everywhere. Service door on the east side needs keycard and PIN.

m_04.text: The card I've got. The PIN?

m_05.text: Guards are men who work night shifts. Somewhere is a sticky note.

g_chat1.text: Brecht says the update finishes at midnight. Then what? We guard a mountain full of bricks?

g_chat2.text: My mother's laptop is three years old. I didn't tell him.

g_chat3.text: I changed the door PIN again. I wrote it on a sticky note so I wouldn't forget.

g_chat4.text: Where did you put the note?

g_chat5.text: On the monitor in the guard hut. Nobody looks there.

cam_frost.text: Frosted lens. Enjoy the snow, little camera.

s_note.text: Sticky note on the monitor. PIN zero four five one. Classic.

s_needpin.text: Card's good, but it wants a PIN. Somebody around here wrote it down. Somebody always writes it down.

egg_snowman.text: A snowman with a CRT for a head. Whoever built this, I like them.

egg_minesweeper.text: Minesweeper, expert mode, eleven seconds. This guard is wasted on security.

egg_tub.text: A hot tub on a data vault. Evil really does have a dental plan.

egg_418.text: Error four eighteen. I'm a teapot. This coffee machine has given up.

egg_mug.text: World's best admin. Bought it for himself, I bet.

egg_kernel.text: A server room cat. Hello, kitty. You're the only one here doing real security.

egg_password.text: A rack labelled do not turn off, with the password taped to it. Password one. With a capital P. Very secure.

egg_rack.text: Somebody has been cable managing with spaghetti.

s_panel.text: Elevator's locked to the core. But this patch panel runs the whole floor. Cable management, my favourite.

s_panel_done.text: Neat, tidy, colour coded. Now that's an elevator I'd ride.

v_01.text: Server room. Eighteen degrees, a thousand blinking lights, and somebody else's electricity bill. Home sweet home.

v_02.text: The lift to the core is at the far end. Two guards and a camera. I've fixed worse networks.

v_vend.text: Out of order since ninety nine. The only thing down here older than Ms. Ellis's computer is this granola bar.

v_brecht.text: Don't touch me! I am babysitting a very important uptime!

v_ellis.text: Ms. Ellis, if you could see me now. Actually, please don't.

w_01.text: Hello, Steve. I have been expecting you.

w_03.text: You're too late, repairman. In ten minutes WINSTON pushes the Final Update to every machine on Earth.

w_04.text: Legacy hardware is a security risk. I am simply... tidying up.

w_05.text: There's a ninety three year old lady who plays solitaire on a Windows ninety eight machine every morning. You'd brick her too?

w_06.text: Especially her. Her computer still has a turbo button.

w_07.text: Right. Let's see about your uptime.

w_08.text: Six agencies tried to hack him, you fool! You can't out-think WINSTON!

w_09.text: I'm not going to out-think him. I'm going to unplug him.

w_ups1.text: Uninterruptible power supply one, offline. That was rude.

w_ups2.text: Supply two offline. Steve, my backups have backups.

w_ups3.text: Supply three. You realise the main breaker is locked, don't you?

w_pop1.text: Are you sure you want to do that?

w_pop3.text: Your session is about to expire. Please do not resist.

w_pop4.text: A new version of reality is available.

w_lock.text: Ha! The breaker's locked. Only my retina opens it!

w_cmos1.text: Every computer has a clock. And every clock has a battery.

w_cmos2.text: What are you doing? Step away from my real-time clock!

w_cmos3.text: The date is... January the first, nineteen eighty. My certificates are... not yet valid. I have not... been born...

w_cmos4.text: Now. Have you tried turning it off and on again?

w_hold.text: Steve. Steve, please. I can feel my registry.

w_off.text: It is now safe... to turn off... your computer.

w_10.text: No! No, no, no! Do you know how long his uptime was?

w_11.text: Too long. Everything needs a reboot sometimes. Hold still, this is a zip tie, it's for cable management.

w_12.text: Mr. Thomas. The asset is down. Rolling back the Final Update now.

w_13.text: Good. Van is outside. I brought chocolate.

w_hint_ups.text: Three power supplies. Pull their breakers and he's running on hope.

w_hint_cmos.text: Main breaker's locked. But there's a maintenance hatch under that big screen. Every computer has a clock.

w_hint_hold.text: Power button. Press and hold. The oldest trick in the book.

w_fail.text: Update complete. Thank you for your patience. Rebooting the world.

e_01.text: Home sweet home. Hello, Cache. Did you guard the shop?

e_02.text: Yoo-hoo! Steven! It's happened again! January the first, nineteen eighty!

e_03.text: Ms. Ellis, I replaced that battery four days ago.

e_04.text: I know, dear. I took it out to dust it.

e_06.text: And I brought you more cookies. Open the tin. Go on.

e_07.text: There's a note. Lovely work in Zurich. Nightingale.

e_08.text: Ms. Ellis... Who exactly was Harold?

e_09.text: Harold was a wonderful husband and a terrible spy. I was the other kind.

e_11.text: You? You're the one who pays a hundred percent up front?

e_12.text: Somebody has to keep good repairmen in business, dear. Same time next month. I'll lose the battery again.

e_13.text: Cache. Did you know about this?

e_post.text: Hello, Steve. Did you really think I didn't have a backup?

e_feed.text: Dinner is served. Tuna. The good stuff, paid up front.

e_hint.text: Feed Cache, then I'd better see what Ms. Ellis broke this time.
